science.title: Why chaga earns its name
science.text: Chaga grows on birch trees in the cold northern forests and is one of the most antioxidant-dense foods ever measured. Those antioxidants — along with its immune-supporting beta-glucan polysaccharides — are why chaga has been prized for centuries. We standardize ours to 40% polysaccharides so every capsule delivers a meaningful, consistent dose.

format.title: Chaga without the bitter brew
format.text: Traditionally chaga is simmered for hours into a bitter tea. We concentrate it into two clean vegan capsules — all the antioxidants and polysaccharides, none of the brewing or the taste.

items.q: What is chaga and what's it good for?
items.a: Chaga is a mushroom that grows on birch trees and is one of the most antioxidant-rich foods known. It's traditionally used to support the immune system and fight everyday oxidative stress.
It means each batch is standardized so 40% of the chaga is the beneficial polysaccharides (400 mg per serving) — the immune-supporting compounds — for a consistent dose every time.
No — unlike coffee or some energy mushrooms, chaga is non-stimulating and caffeine-free, so you can take it any time of day.

items.q: When will I notice a difference?
items.a: Antioxidant and immune support is cumulative — most people take it daily for a few weeks to feel the benefit.
